intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a cheap souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk to fuel up after your journey.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a snack at the airport — a tyropita (cheese pie) from a bakery kiosk for around €2
meals.dinner: Street souvlaki wrap (pita gyros) near Monastiraki Square — budget €3–5 per wrap

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Use the Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki station for about €9 — it's the most straightforward and budget-friendly option. Validate your ticket before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the heat. Admission is €20 standard, but explore free viewpoints from Filopappou Hill if budget is very tight. Walk through the ancient Agora ruins just below the Acropolis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Monastiraki Flea Market for local crafts, vintage finds, and people-watching. Head to the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street to see fresh produce, spices, meat, and fish stalls — a true local food experience at no cost to browse.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Psiri neighborhood for affordable taverna dining. Enjoy a sit-down meal of moussaka or pastitsio with a glass of house wine.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and Greek coffee at a local bakery near your hostel — €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh spanakopita and a small salad from the Central Market area bakeries — €4–5
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Psiri — moussaka, bread, and a carafe of house wine for €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Athens involves a lot of uphill walking around the Acropolis area. Carry a reusable water bottle; tap water is safe to drink in Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early KTEL bus or ferry from Piraeus port to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour by ferry, €8–10 round trip). Explore the charming port town, visit the local fish market, and walk the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (€5–8/day) or take a local bus to Aegina's beautiful beaches — Agia Marina beach is a popular, clean sandy beach with calm, clear water. Swim and relax through the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by evening ferry. Have dinner near Piraeus port or back in central Athens at a budget eatery.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café near your hostel — €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a simple waterfront taverna in Aegina port — €8–12
meals.dinner: Souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and fries at a local grill house — €7–9

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is a perfect budget day trip from Athens. Check ferry schedules in advance at the Piraeus port or online. The island is also famous for its pistachios — buy a small bag as a local snack.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by KTEL bus to Nafplio (about 2.5 hours, €14 one way) — a stunning coastal town in the Peloponnese. Check into a budget guesthouse and drop your bags.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's charming old town with its Venetian architecture, narrow cobblestone streets, and waterfront promenade (Bourtzi). Climb the 999 steps to Palamidi Fortress for panoramic views of the Argolic Gulf — admission €8.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the seaside promenade and enjoy the sunset. Dine at a local taverna in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee from a street vendor before the bus — €2
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with local bread, olives, feta, and tomatoes from a mini-market — €5
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood mezedes (small plates) at a waterfront taverna in Nafplio — €10–14

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is considered one of Greece's most romantic and picturesque towns. It's a great base for exploring the wider Peloponnese region. Book your guesthouse in advance as it's a popular destination.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi to the ancient site of Epidaurus (about 30 km from Nafplio, bus €3–4 each way). Visit the remarkably preserved ancient theater — one of the best in the world — and the sanctuary of Asclepius.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach, a small rocky beach just a short walk from the old town — free entry, clean water, and beautiful scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nafplio's evening atmosphere — locals come out for their evening 'volta' (stroll). Try local street food or a budget taverna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and tiropita at a local café in Nafplio — €3–4
meals.lunch: Simple gyros or souvlaki wrap from a local grill near the bus station — €3–5
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb chops (paidakia) with village salad and bread at a local taverna — €12–15

day_by_day.notes: The Epidaurus theater has incredible acoustics — even a whisper from the stage can be heard at the top row. If visiting in late June, check if there are any evening performances at the Epidaurus Festival.

day_by_day.morning: Travel by KTEL bus from Nafplio to Patras (about 3 hours, €15–18), then take a ferry or bus connection to Kefalonia island. Alternatively, travel to the port of Killini and take a ferry to Zakynthos (about 1 hour, €8–10). Arrive and check into a budget hostel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in and explore the main town (Zakynthos Town or Argostoli if on Kefalonia). Visit the local market and waterfront. Relax at a nearby town beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local waterfront tavernas and enjoy the island's relaxed evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pastry and coffee at a bakery before departure — €3
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a quick bite at the ferry port — €4–6
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a simple waterfront taverna — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Travel day — keep snacks and water handy. Ferry and bus connections in Greece can sometimes run late, so build in buffer time. Zakynthos is famous for its stunning beaches and sea turtles.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a scooter (€15–20/day) to explore the island's famous beaches. On Zakynthos, head to Gerakas Beach — a protected loggerhead sea turtle nesting beach with crystal-clear turquoise water and golden sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Porto Zoro or Banana Beach — both beautiful, less crowded beaches on the southeastern coast. Swim, snorkel, and soak up the sun. Average temperature of 23°C makes for perfect beach weather.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town for dinner. Try local Zakynthian specialties like sofrito (veal in white wine sauce) or skordalia.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and fruit at a café — €4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local supermarket — bread, cheese, olives, fruit — €5–6
meals.dinner: Local taverna with Zakynthian specialties — sofrito or fresh fish — €11–14

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has restricted hours in the morning during turtle nesting season (June–August) — arrive after 9:00 AM. Do not disturb nesting areas marked with signs. Renting a scooter is the most budget-friendly way to explore the island independently.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget boat tour around Zakynthos (€15–20) to visit the famous Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach — only accessible by boat — and the stunning Blue Caves. Book through a local agency for the best price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat tour and spend the afternoon relaxing at a local beach near town. Explore the Zakynthos Town waterfront and Byzantine Museum (€4 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final evening on Zakynthos with dinner at a budget taverna. Try local wine (Verdea) produced on the island.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri and coffee before the boat tour — €2–3
meals.lunch: Snacks on the boat or a quick bite at the port upon return — €5–7
meals.dinner: Mezedes spread (tzatziki, taramosalata, grilled vegetables, pita) at a local taverna — €9–12

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is one of the most photographed spots in Greece — the boat tour is absolutely worth the cost. Book the tour the evening before to secure a spot. The Blue Caves are best visited in the morning when the light is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Zakynthos back to Killini on the mainland, then connect by bus to Athens (total travel approximately 4–5 hours). Alternatively, take a domestic flight if budget allows (check Ryanair or Sky Express for deals under €40).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Athens and take the Metro or bus to Piraeus port. Board an afternoon ferry to Santorini (about 5–8 hours by standard ferry, €35–50; or high-speed ferry in 4.5 hours for €60–80). Arrive in Santorini by evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget hostel in Fira or Perissa. Take a short walk to get oriented and grab a simple dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pastry and coffee before departure — €3
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — bring your own food from a supermarket to save money — €4–5
meals.dinner: Simple gyros or souvlaki near the hostel in Fira or Perissa — €5–7

day_by_day.notes: This is a heavy travel day. Book ferry tickets in advance online (ferryscanner.com or directferries.gr) to get the best prices. Standard ferries are significantly cheaper than high-speed options and still comfortable for overnight or long journeys.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Fira, Santorini's main town, on foot. Walk the caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli for stunning volcanic caldera views — completely free. Visit the Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral and browse the local streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus (€1.80) to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the south coast — famous for its unique black volcanic sand. Swim and relax on the beach. The water is clear and the black sand retains heat beautifully.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Santorini sunset from Fira's caldera viewpoint (free alternative to the crowded Oia). Have dinner at a budget taverna away from the tourist-heavy main streets.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local tomatoes, and feta from a mini-market — €4
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki at a local grill near Perissa Beach — €4–6
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled octopus and village salad at a local taverna in Fira — €12–15

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is one of Greece's pricier islands, but costs can be managed by eating away from the main tourist strips, using local buses instead of taxis, and choosing accommodation in Perissa or Kamari rather than Oia or Fira clifftop.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Oia village (€1.80) in the morning before the crowds arrive. Walk the famous blue-domed streets, browse local art galleries, and enjoy the dramatic caldera views. Visit the Venetian Castle ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the scenic caldera trail from Oia back to Fira (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) — one of the most spectacular free hikes in Greece with continuous caldera and sea views. Alternatively, take the bus back and visit Akrotiri Archaeological Site (€12 entry) — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age city buried by volcanic eruption.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Red Beach near Akrotiri — a dramatic beach with red and black volcanic cliffs. Return to your hostel and enjoy a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a cheese pie at a local bakery in Fira — €3–4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the hike — local bread, olives, cheese, and fruit from a mini-market — €5–6
meals.dinner: Moussaka and a glass of local Assyrtiko wine at a budget taverna — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: The Oia to Fira hike is best done in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and carry plenty of water. The trail is well-marked but can be rocky in places — wear proper shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (approximately 2–3 hours by high-speed ferry, €40–55) or choose a slower, cheaper option. Arrive in Mykonos and check into a budget hostel. Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) — the iconic whitewashed windmills, Little Venice, and narrow labyrinthine streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus (€2) to Paradise Beach or Platis Gialos Beach — two of Mykonos's most popular beaches with clear turquoise water. Swim and relax. Avoid the beach clubs (expensive) and find a free spot on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the atmospheric Little Venice neighborhood at sunset. Have dinner at a budget taverna away from the main tourist drag.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee before the ferry — €3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap from a local grill in Mykonos Town — €4–5
meals.dinner: Fresh fish soup (kakavia) and grilled sardines at a simple local taverna — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is known as one of Greece's most expensive islands. Save money by eating at local gyros shops rather than restaurants, using public buses instead of taxis, and avoiding the famous beach clubs. The island's beauty is free to enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final morning exploring Mykonos Town at a leisurely pace. Visit the Folklore Museum (free or minimal entry) and the famous Mykonos windmills for photos. Browse the local market for affordable souvenirs — local thyme honey, dried herbs, or small ceramic pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Agios Sostis Beach — one of Mykonos's most beautiful and least commercialized beaches, accessible by a short walk or taxi. No sunbeds or beach clubs — just natural beauty and clear water. A perfect final afternoon in Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos port for your departure ferry or flight back to Athens for your connecting flight home. Enjoy a final Greek coffee and a piece of baklava at the port before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a local café — yogurt, honey, bread, eggs, and coffee — €6–8 (treat yourself on the last day!)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Agios Sostis Beach — local bread, feta, tomatoes, and olives from a mini-market — €5–6
meals.dinner: Final souvlaki or gyros wrap at the port before departure — €4–5

day_by_day.notes: Check your return ferry or flight schedule carefully and arrive at the port or airport with plenty of time. Mykonos Airport has connections to Athens (Sky Express, Olympic Air) for approximately €40–70 if you need to fly back. Book return transport in advance to secure the best budget prices.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Plaka neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle stroll through the charming Plaka district to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Monastiraki Flea Market area as the evening crowds gather. Enjoy your first Greek dinner at a traditional taverna in Plaka, soaking in the ambiance of the old city beneath the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a street kiosk near the airport or in central Athens after check-in (€4–7)
meals.dinner: Taverna Lysikratous or similar traditional taverna in Plaka — try moussaka, tzatziki, and a Greek salad with local house wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. The Metro from the airport to Syntagma takes about 40 minutes and costs €9. Exchange some euros at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) before the heat and crowds build. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and the Propylaea. Purchase a combined ticket (€30) that also covers several other archaeological sites in Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-class Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill — it houses stunning original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis site. Afterward, walk to the Ancient Agora of Athens, the heart of ancient Greek civic life, and explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the vibrant Monastiraki and Psiri neighborhoods for evening drinks and dinner. Explore the lively squares and rooftop bars with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Plaka — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh orange juice, and a freddo espresso (€6–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Acropolis Museum café with a view — salads, sandwiches, and mezze platters (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Monastiraki such as Couleur Locale or similar — enjoy grilled octopus, fava dip, and fresh fish with Acropolis views (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen and a hat. The Acropolis involves significant uphill walking on uneven marble surfaces. Book Acropolis Museum entry online in advance to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum of Athens, one of the greatest museums in the world, housing treasures from across ancient Greece including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold artifacts. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and walk up Lycabettus Hill (by funicular or on foot) for panoramic 360-degree views over Athens and the Saronic Gulf. Afterward, browse the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) for a sensory immersion into local food culture — olives, spices, fresh fish, and meats.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening food tour or explore the Exarchia and Kolonaki neighborhoods for dinner. Try a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) for a social, sharing-style Greek meal.

meals.breakfast: Bakery breakfast near your hotel — tiropita (cheese pie), koulouri (sesame bread ring), and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Eat at the Central Market area — fresh souvlaki, grilled meats, or a hearty bean soup (fasolada) at a local workers' taverna (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio in Exarchia or Kolonaki — order a spread of mezedes: dolmades, saganaki, grilled halloumi, taramasalata, and local Assyrtiko wine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — Wednesday through Monday it opens at 8:00 AM. The Varvakios Market is most lively in the morning; try to visit before 1:00 PM for the best atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by ferry from Piraeus Port to Santorini (approximately 5–8 hours by standard ferry, or 2 hours by high-speed catamaran). Book the high-speed option for comfort. Enjoy the Aegean Sea views from the deck as you approach the dramatic caldera of Santorini.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini (Thira). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani. Take the cable car up from the port to Fira town. Explore the winding whitewashed streets of Fira, browse local shops, and visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the caldera-edge path from Fira toward Firostefani for stunning sunset views over the volcanic caldera. Enjoy dinner at a caldera-view restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Athens hotel before heading to Piraeus (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the ferry or eat at the ferry's onboard café — sandwiches, pastries, and coffee (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range caldera-view restaurant in Fira — try fresh grilled sea bream, Santorinian fava (yellow split pea dip), and local Vinsanto wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June travel — Santorini is extremely popular. The high-speed catamaran (SeaJets or Hellenic Seaways) costs approximately €60–80 one way. Fira is very walkable but has steep steps — pack light for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Rent an ATV or hire a local taxi to explore the island. Visit the iconic village of Oia in the morning before the crowds arrive — wander its blue-domed churches, narrow alleys, and art galleries. Explore the Oia Castle ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kamari Beach or Perissa Beach on the eastern coast — Santorini's famous black volcanic sand beaches. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, swim in the clear Aegean waters, and relax. The black sand gets very hot, so wear sandals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the world-famous Santorini sunset — arrive at least an hour early to secure a good viewing spot. The sunset from Oia Castle is legendary. Enjoy dinner in Oia afterward.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café in Fira — Greek yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and freddo cappuccino (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Kamari or Perissa — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia after sunset — try a mid-range restaurant serving Santorinian specialties like white eggplant, cherry tomato fritters, and fresh lobster pasta (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Oia at sunset is extremely crowded in June — arrive by 7:00 PM for a good spot. ATV rental costs approximately €25–35 per day. Perissa Beach has more budget-friendly tavernas than Kamari. Wear reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning volcano and hot springs boat tour from Fira's old port (Ammoudi Bay). Visit the active Nea Kameni volcanic island, hike to the crater, and swim in the natural sulfuric hot springs. A truly unique Santorini experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient ruins of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption around 1600 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' The site is covered and air-conditioned, perfect for the afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed final evening in Santorini. Explore the local wine scene — visit a winery such as Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas for a tasting of indigenous Assyrtiko and Nykteri wines with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat tour — pastries and coffee from a local bakery in Fira (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch back in Fira after the tour — try a local gyros shop or a casual mezedopoleio (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Wine and mezedes dinner at Santo Wines winery or a nearby restaurant — cheese platters, cured meats, and local wines (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The volcano boat tour costs approximately €20–25 per person and departs multiple times daily from the old port. Book Akrotiri tickets online (€12 entry). The winery visit is a great way to spend a relaxed Sunday evening — Santo Wines has spectacular sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Santorini to Zakynthos (via Athens or direct seasonal routes — check schedules). Alternatively, fly from Santorini to Zakynthos via Athens (approximately 2–3 hours total with connection). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Zakynthos Town or Laganas area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After arriving and settling in, visit Zakynthos Town (Chora) — explore the Venetian-influenced architecture, the Byzantine Museum, and the main Solomos Square. Walk along the harbor promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first evening in Zakynthos. Explore the local tavernas along the harbor for fresh Ionian seafood.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Santorini hotel before departure (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Airport or ferry snacks, or a quick meal upon arrival in Zakynthos (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Harborside taverna in Zakynthos Town — try fresh grilled octopus, bourdeto (spicy fish stew), and local Verdea white wine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Inter-island travel in Greece can be complex — flying via Athens is often the most reliable option. Book flights or ferries well in advance. The journey may take most of the morning and early afternoon depending on connections. Zakynthos is in the Ionian Sea, west of mainland Greece.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour to the iconic **Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach)** — one of Greece's most photographed and spectacular beaches. The only way to reach it is by boat from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town. The turquoise water enclosed by towering white limestone cliffs is absolutely breathtaking. Swim and explore the famous rusting shipwreck on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour to the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos — sea caves where the water glows an ethereal electric blue due to light refraction. Swim inside the caves for an unforgettable experience. Return to your hotel by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and enjoy the sunset from a clifftop viewpoint above Navagio Beach (accessible by road) for a different perspective. Dinner in a local village taverna.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café — Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the boat tour, or eat at a small beach café near Porto Vromi before/after the tour (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Traditional village taverna in Anafonitria or Volimes — try sofrito (veal in white wine sauce), fresh grilled fish, and local wine (€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Navagio Beach boat tour costs approximately €15–25 per person depending on the operator. Tours typically depart in the morning. Bring waterproof sunscreen, a towel, and water shoes. The beach has no shade — the cliffs provide some relief. Book the boat tour the day before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Laganas Beach and the surrounding area — Zakynthos is home to one of the most important loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting sites in the Mediterranean. Take a responsible sea turtle watching boat tour in the morning to spot these magnificent creatures in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the inland villages of Zakynthos — visit Machairado with its beautiful church, and the village of Keri for its lighthouse and dramatic clifftop views over the Ionian Sea. Stop at local honey and olive oil producers along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos Town for a final evening on the island. Visit the Venetian Castle above the town for panoramic views, then enjoy a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bakery breakfast in Laganas — tiropita, spanakopita, and Greek coffee (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a village café in Keri or Machairado — simple Greek salad, grilled meats, and local bread (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Zakynthos Town — try mandolato (local nougat) for dessert and sample local Zakynthian cuisine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle watching tours must be conducted responsibly — choose operators certified by the Sea Turtle Protection Society of Greece (ARCHELON). Do not touch or disturb the turtles. Laganas Bay is a protected National Marine Park.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Zakynthos to Heraklion, Crete (via Athens if necessary — approximately 2–3 hours total). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Heraklion or Chania. If arriving in Heraklion, visit the impressive Heraklion Archaeological Museum, home to the world's finest collection of Minoan art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Bronze Age palace of the Minoan civilization, associated with the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth. Explore the remarkably reconstructed ruins with a local guide for context.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's vibrant old town — walk along the Venetian harbor, visit the Koules Fortress, and browse the lively market street (1866 Street) for local products.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Zakynthos hotel before departure (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Knossos — local taverna serving Cretan specialties like dakos (barley rusk salad) and grilled lamb (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Cretan restaurant in Heraklion old town — try lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), Cretan cheese, and local Vidiano wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Knossos entry costs €15 (or €20 with the Archaeological Museum combined ticket). A guided tour is highly recommended to understand the site's complex history. Crete is Greece's largest island with a distinct culinary tradition — embrace the local Cretan diet, considered one of the healthiest in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning drive or bus to **Elafonissi Beach** in southwestern Crete — one of Greece's most stunning beaches, famous for its pink-tinged sand (colored by crushed coral and shells) and shallow, crystal-clear turquoise lagoon. The drive takes approximately 1.5–2 hours from Heraklion or 1 hour from Chania.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Elafonissi — swim in the shallow lagoon, walk across the sandbar to the small island of Elafonissi, explore the dunes, and relax on the pink sand. The water is exceptionally clear and calm, making it ideal for snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Chania (if basing yourself there) or Heraklion. Stop in the charming old Venetian town of Chania for dinner — one of Crete's most beautiful cities with a stunning harbor.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — Cretan honey, fresh bread, and local cheese at your hotel or a roadside café (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna near Elafonissi — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold drinks (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Chania Venetian harbor — try fresh seafood, Cretan lamb, and local raki (Cretan spirit) at a harborside restaurant (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is very popular in June — arrive early (before 10:00 AM) to secure a good spot and avoid the worst of the crowds. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snorkeling gear. The beach has limited shade. Car rental in Crete costs approximately €30–50 per day and is highly recommended for flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km, cutting through the White Mountains (Lefka Ori) of western Crete. The hike takes 4–6 hours and ends at the coastal village of Agia Roumeli. The scenery is spectacular with towering rock walls, wildflowers, and mountain streams.
day_by_day.afternoon: Upon completing the gorge hike, arrive at Agia Roumeli beach — a remote, pristine beach accessible only by boat or on foot. Take a refreshing swim in the Libyan Sea to cool down after the hike. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (approximately 1 hour), then bus or taxi back to your base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania or Heraklion. Enjoy a well-deserved relaxing dinner celebrating your gorge achievement. Explore the evening atmosphere of Chania's old town.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before the gorge — energy-rich foods: eggs, bread, cheese, and fruit (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch for the gorge — energy bars, nuts, fruit, and plenty of water (prepare the night before)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Cretan taverna — slow-roasted lamb (kleftiko), horta (wild greens), and a carafe of local wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is open from May to October. Entry fee is €5. Wear sturdy hiking shoes — the terrain is rocky. Bring at least 2 liters of water per person, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the cool gorge interior. The total journey (gorge + ferry + bus) takes a full day. Book the return ferry in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete — visit the Chania Municipal Market (Agora) for a last immersion in Greek food culture. Stock up on local products to take home: Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, local cheeses (graviera, anthotyros), and Cretan rusks. Browse the stalls and chat with local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final swim at a nearby beach — Falasarna Beach near Chania is one of Crete's finest, with golden sand and clear water. Alternatively, take a final stroll through Chania's old town, visit the Maritime Museum, and enjoy a last coffee at a harborside café.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Heraklion or Chania airport for your return flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring Greece's beaches, ancient history, and extraordinary food culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a Chania café — full spread of local cheeses, olives, honey, yogurt, and coffee (€10–14)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach taverna at Falasarna or a café in Chania old town — dakos salad, fresh juice, and a last gyros (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or an early dinner before departure — or pack some local pastries and snacks from the market for the journey home (€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Heraklion Airport (HER) and Chania Airport (CHQ) are both well-connected. Liquid restrictions apply for olive oil and wine in carry-on luggage — pack these in checked baggage. Keep your combined Athens archaeological site ticket as a wonderful souvenir.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your hotel in central Athens. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll through the Plaka neighborhood to begin soaking in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening walk through Monastiraki Square and the illuminated Acropolis viewpoints. Settle into the city's rhythm with a glass of local wine at a rooftop bar overlooking the Acropolis.

meals.breakfast: Meal on board or at the airport
meals.lunch: Meal on board or at the airport
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant — a classic Athenian taverna with a stunning Acropolis view; try the lamb kleftiko and grilled octopus with a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. No heavy sightseeing on arrival day — prioritize rest and acclimatization. Athens average high is around 23°C, perfect for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and heat. Book a skip-the-line private guided tour for an in-depth historical experience. Follow with a visit to the Acropolis Museum, one of Europe's finest archaeological museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Athens Central Market Food Tour — explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local spice vendors, olive oil producers, cheese mongers, and fresh seafood stalls. Sample cured meats, local cheeses, honey, and freshly baked bread with a knowledgeable local food guide.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for boutique shopping and aperitifs. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a traditional kafeneio — Greek yogurt with Cretan thyme honey, fresh fruit, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts)
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch during the food tour — graze on market finds including taramosalata, spanakopita, and fresh olives
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside — Michelin-starred seafood restaurant by chef Lefteris Lazarou; signature dishes include sea urchin pasta and grilled John Dory with capers

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and Varoulko Seaside well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the food tour. The market is most lively between 7:00 AM and 2:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum, the largest archaeological museum in Greece, housing treasures including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold artifacts. Arrange a private guided tour for a premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ancient Agora of Athens and the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Wander through the charming Thissio neighborhood with its neoclassical architecture and café-lined pedestrian streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Athens Riviera (Glyfada area) for a sunset swim at a premium beach bar, followed by dinner overlooking the Saronic Gulf.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit a traditional bakery for tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Avissinia in Monastiraki — traditional Greek cuisine in a charming antique-market setting; try the slow-cooked lamb with orzo
meals.dinner: Dinner at Island Club Restaurant in Varkiza — glamorous open-air seafood restaurant on the Athens Riviera with fresh catch of the day and premium Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — confirm opening hours. Taxi or rideshare to Glyfada takes approximately 30 minutes from central Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens for Mykonos via a short domestic flight (approximately 45 minutes) or high-speed ferry from Piraeus. Check into a luxury clifftop hotel in Mykonos Town (Chora). Take a morning stroll through the iconic whitewashed alleys of Chora, visiting the famous windmills and Little Venice waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Experience — spend the afternoon at Psarou Beach, one of Mykonos's most exclusive beaches, with premium sun loungers, crystal-clear turquoise water, and world-class beach club service. Enjoy water sports or simply relax in the Aegean sun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the famous sunset at Little Venice. Explore the boutique shops and art galleries before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before travel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nammos Beach Restaurant at Psarou Beach — one of the most celebrated beach restaurants in Greece; try the fresh lobster pasta and grilled sea bass
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobu Mykonos or M-eating Restaurant in Chora — contemporary Greek cuisine with premium local ingredients; try the tuna tartare with Santorini capers and grilled lamb chops

day_by_day.notes: Book Psarou Beach sun loungers in advance during June — they sell out quickly. Consider a private speedboat transfer from Athens for a more luxurious arrival experience. Pack reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private boat excursion to the sacred island of Delos — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important archaeological sites in the Aegean. Explore the ancient ruins, including the iconic Terrace of the Lions, with a private archaeologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and relax at Paradise Beach — a legendary beach with vibrant energy, golden sand, and warm shallow waters. Enjoy a premium beach club experience with cocktails and light bites.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar in Chora, followed by a leisurely dinner in the atmospheric old town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, Greek yogurt, local honey, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a beach club at Paradise Beach — grilled halloumi, tzatziki, fresh pita, and Greek salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spilia Seaside Restaurant — a dramatic cave-set restaurant carved into the cliffs; fresh seafood and local Cycladic wines

day_by_day.notes: Delos is only accessible by boat and closes in the afternoon — depart by 9:00 AM. The site has no shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen, and water. Delos is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mykonos for Santorini via high-speed ferry (approximately 2 hours) or short flight. Check into a luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli with a private plunge pool and caldera views. Explore the iconic blue-domed churches and winding paths of Oia village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private catamaran sailing tour around the Santorini caldera, visiting the volcanic hot springs at Nea Kameni, the red and white beaches, and snorkeling in crystal-clear waters. Champagne and fresh fruit served on board.
day_by_day.evening: Position yourself at the famous Oia Castle viewpoint for Santorini's legendary sunset — one of the most spectacular in the world. Enjoy champagne as the sun dips below the caldera.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before travel
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served on the catamaran — fresh seafood, Greek salads, local cheeses, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites in Oia — fine dining with panoramic caldera views; try the Santorini fava with truffle and the slow-roasted lamb

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran tour and dinner reservations well in advance — June is peak season in Santorini. The Oia sunset area gets extremely crowded; arrive at least 45 minutes early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by a volcanic eruption around 1600 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Arrange a private guided tour for the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the unique Red Beach and White Beach near Akrotiri — dramatic volcanic landscapes with striking colored cliffs. Relax on the black sand of Perissa or Perivolos Beach with premium beach club facilities in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting tour at one of Santorini's prestigious wineries — visit Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas for a guided tasting of indigenous Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto wines with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — enjoy your private terrace with caldera views, fresh local tomatoes, Santorini fava, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia — a beloved local taverna known for authentic Santorinian cuisine; try the tomato keftedes (fritters) and grilled fresh fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — one of Santorini's most acclaimed restaurants celebrating local terroir; tasting menu featuring Santorini cherry tomatoes, white eggplant, and local capers

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. Red Beach access involves a short rocky walk — wear sturdy sandals. The winery tour is best arranged for late afternoon to coincide with sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Santorini for Crete via ferry or short flight to Heraklion or Chania. Check into a luxury boutique hotel in Chania's Venetian harbor area. Explore the stunning Venetian harbor, the historic lighthouse, and the atmospheric old town with its mix of Venetian, Ottoman, and Greek architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class — join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (Cretan bruschetta), stuffed zucchini flowers, slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades. Visit a local market beforehand to select fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Venetian harbor at dusk and enjoy the magical atmosphere of the old town's lit-up mosques, fountains, and narrow alleys.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before travel
meals.lunch: Lunch prepared and enjoyed during the cooking class — a full Cretan feast with local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tamam Restaurant in Chania — housed in a converted Ottoman bathhouse; try the Cretan lamb with artichokes and the local cheese platter with thyme honey

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — premium classes with market visits fill up quickly. Chania's old town is best explored on foot. The Venetian harbor is particularly beautiful at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip — depart early by private car (approximately 1.5 hours from Chania) to visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and shells, shallow turquoise lagoons, and dramatic natural scenery. Arrive early to secure the best spot before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Elafonissi — wade through the shallow pink lagoon, explore the small island accessible on foot, and snorkel in the clear waters. The beach is part of a protected nature reserve with unique flora.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania by private car. Freshen up and explore the covered market (Agora) of Chania for local products — olive oil, herbs, honey, and Cretan cheeses to take home.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — Cretan rusks with olive oil and tomato, local cheese, and mountain tea
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the beach — arrange a premium picnic basket with the hotel featuring local cheeses, charcuterie, olives, fresh bread, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Thalassino Ageri in Chania — a romantic seafood restaurant perched above the sea; try the grilled lobster with lemon butter and the fresh catch of the day

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is a protected nature reserve — no umbrellas can be staked in the sand in certain areas. Bring your own shade. Arrive by 9:00 AM to avoid crowds. The drive passes through stunning Cretan mountain villages.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palace of Knossos near Heraklion — the largest Bronze Age archaeological site in Crete and the legendary home of King Minos and the Minotaur. Arrange a private expert guide for a comprehensive tour of this 3,500-year-old Minoan palace complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Heraklion Archaeological Museum — one of the most important museums in Greece, housing the world's finest collection of Minoan art including the famous Bull-Leaping Fresco and the Phaistos Disc. Return to Chania by private car along the scenic northern coastal road.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening in Chania — visit the Firkas Venetian Fortress for panoramic harbor views, then browse the artisan shops in the old town for handmade leather goods, ceramics, and local olive wood products.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional kafeneio in Heraklion — try the Cretan salad with graviera cheese, fresh tomatoes, and barley rusks, plus a glass of local Vidiano white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Portes Restaurant in Chania old town — intimate setting in a restored Venetian building; try the slow-braised goat with Cretan herbs and the wild greens pie

day_by_day.notes: Knossos is approximately 1.5 hours from Chania — depart by 8:30 AM. Book private guide in advance. The Heraklion Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — verify schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Crete for Zakynthos (Zante) via connecting flight through Athens. Check into a luxury clifftop resort on the island. Explore the charming Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) with its Venetian-influenced architecture, the Byzantine Museum, and the main square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Boat Tour — take a private or small-group boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. Accessible only by sea, this stunning cove features a rusting shipwreck (the MV Panagiotis) on white pebble sand surrounded by towering white limestone cliffs and impossibly blue water. Swim and snorkel in the crystal-clear cove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a sunset from the clifftop viewpoint above Navagio Beach (accessible by road) for a dramatic aerial perspective of the shipwreck cove.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before travel
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the boat or at a waterfront taverna in Porto Vromi before the Navagio excursion
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malanos Restaurant in Zakynthos Town — a beloved local institution serving traditional Zakynthian cuisine; try the sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce) and the local mandolato nougat for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach boat tours depart from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos harbor. Book a private boat for the most premium experience. The clifftop viewpoint is accessible by car/taxi and offers spectacular photography opportunities — best at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Sea turtle snorkeling and boat tour around Zakynthos — visit the Laganas Bay area, a protected habitat for the endangered loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta). Take a responsible eco-certified boat tour to observe turtles in their natural habitat. Also visit the stunning Blue Caves on the northern tip of the island, where sunlight refracts through the water creating magical blue hues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at one of Zakynthos's premium beaches — Gerakas Beach (a protected turtle nesting beach with pristine sand) or Porto Zoro Beach with its crystal-clear waters and dramatic rock formations. Enjoy a premium beach club experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Zakynthos — explore the local shops for Zakynthian specialties including mandolato (nougat), pasteli (sesame honey bars), and local olive oil. Enjoy a farewell cocktail at a clifftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — fresh local pastries, Greek yogurt with Zakynthian honey, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at a waterfront taverna in Agios Nikolaos village — grilled fresh fish, Greek salad, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Prosilio Restaurant in Zakynthos Town — elegant setting with a focus on local Ionian cuisine; try the lobster spaghetti and the grilled whole sea bream with capers and lemon

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has restricted access after sunset to protect nesting turtles — respect all conservation guidelines. The Blue Caves are best visited in the morning when the light is optimal. Book the turtle tour with a certified responsible operator.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Zakynthos — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort and take a last swim at the hotel pool or a nearby beach. Pack and prepare for departure. Visit a local bakery or deli to stock up on Greek food souvenirs — local olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, and regional cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Zakynthos Airport (ZTH) for connecting flight back to Athens (ATH) and onward connection to Belgrade via Air Serbia. Allow ample time for connections. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the best of Greece's beaches, cuisine, history, and island life.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens or in-transit — enjoy a final Greek meal at the airport or during the flight.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the resort — a full spread of Greek specialties including tiropita, spanakopita, local cheeses, honey, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the harbor before heading to the airport — fresh salad, grilled vegetables, and local bread
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all return flight times and allow at least 2.5 hours for the Athens connection. Zakynthos Airport is small — arrive 2 hours before departure. Duty-free at Athens airport offers a good selection of Greek wines, olive oils, and spirits as final souvenirs.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
